title: Automate synthetic quality checks on catalog and tenant version changes
creator: Ethan Zhao
description: Problem: When a model in our public catalog is bumped or when a customer pins/updates a model version we currently rely on ad-hoc post-deploy checks and manual smoke runs. That creates variability in detection time for quality regressions and increases customer risk. Goal: Implement an automated, tenant-aware evaluation trigger that runs a prioritized suite of synthetic checks whenever a catalog change or a customer version-pin/upgrade occurs, surface results in Console, and route high-confidence regressions to on-call + customer success.
acceptance_criteria: A catalog model version change (catalog write event) automatically enqueues a pre-configured smoke eval job within 30s
A customer-initiated version pin/upgrade enqueues a tenant-scoped eval job that runs against that customer's pinned prompts/synthetic workload

Eval jobs run using the prioritized profile (smoke -> targeted regression -> full-sample) and write results to the EvalService with metadata: trigger_type, triggering_actor, tenant_id, model_id, model_revision
Failures crossing configured thresholds create an alert in the Console (per-route) and send a Slack incident to #prod-evals and on-call
Console shows a clear pass/fail and regression delta, with links to the failing prompts and PR suggestions for rollback or mitigation
There is a feature flag to disable auto-eval per-tenant and a config to adjust sample size and acceptance thresholds
Telemetry is captured for runtime, cost estimate, and token usage for each triggered eval
success_metrics: Time-to-detection for major regressions reduced from median 8h to <15 minutes for catalog changes
False positive rate for automated eval alerts < 8% measured over a 30 day window
>90% of catalog upgrades and customer pins get at least a smoke eval run by default
Reduction in customer-reported post-upgrade regressions by 30% among early adopters
scope: Deliver an event-driven orchestration that listens to catalog writes and customer pin API events, maps trigger to tenant-specific or catalog eval profiles, and invokes existing EvalRunner with safe resource limits and priority tags. Integrate results into Console and Alerting. Expose per-tenant controls and a global kill-switch.
out_of_scope: Automatic rollback of model pins (this ticket only surfaces alerts and recommended remediation), building new evaluation datasets (we will reuse curated smoke and regression sets), and fine-grained cost accounting for each eval job beyond token estimates.
